questions.q: What is the connect and redirect approach?
a: Connect with the child first, then correct the behavior
Redirect the child before discussing any feelings
Punish first and explain the reason later
Ignore the behavior and distract the child
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes connect and redirect as taking time to connect, then steering the child toward better behavior.

questions.q: What does the summary call the brain region that handles empathy?
a: The upstairs brain
The downstairs brain
The left hemisphere
The survival brain
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the upstairs brain handles empathy and emotion, while the downstairs brain manages basic needs.

questions.q: Why should parents avoid time-outs and spanking, per the summary?
a: They breed resentment and fear
They take too much time to carry out
They teach children to negotiate
They work only on older children
questions.why: Lesson 1 says these punishments create resentment and fear, which helps neither parent nor child.

questions.q: What should a parent do when a toddler melts down in a store?
a: Acknowledge the feelings and connect before redirecting
Give in quickly to stop the screaming
Leave the store without a word
Explain the rules in a long lecture
questions.why: Lesson 2 says not to dismiss feelings; comfort and acknowledgment help engage the upstairs brain.

questions.q: Why should parents search for the why behind misbehavior?
a: Understanding the reason makes redirection easier
It proves the child is lying
It shifts blame onto the child
It delays any consequence indefinitely
questions.why: Lesson 3 says children need to feel understood, and the reason makes redirection much easier.
